sentences.text: 1 .  On 13th May, 2011, the petitioner No.1 was married to the respondent No.2/complainant and both are blessed with a daughter Pranjan, who is aged about ten years.

Out of matrimonial discord alleging ill-treatment, the offence being Crime No. 127 of 2015 came to be registered against the petitioners for the offence punishable under Sections 498A, 324, 504 r/w 34 of IPC.
2.
The respondent No.2/complainant has placed on record consent affidavit thereby extending consent for quashing.

The respondent No.2/complainant in the affidavit has specifically stated that it is agreed between the parties that the custody of the minor daughter Pranjan shall remain with the Manish Mohan Sondarva vs State Of Maharashtra on 16 October, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/30483571/

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Counsel for the petitioners on instructions agrees to the same.

3. In response to the court's query, both the counsels state that in the DV Act proceedings, the petitioner/husband has agreed to pay permanent alimony to the respondent No.2/complainant and also towards the maintenance of the daughter.
Since the statement is also coming from the petitioner/husband, same is accepted as an undertaking to this Court.
In this background, we deem it appropriate to allow the petition.
4. The petition as such stands allowed in terms of prayer clause (a).

[N. R. BORKAR, J.] [NITIN W. SAMBRE, J.]
